---
title: "Valaciclovir - Abdalla et al. 2020"
output: html_document
---

# Population Pharmacokinetics of Intravenous and Oral Acyclovir and Oral Valacyclovir in Pediatric Population To Optimize Dosing Regimens (Abdalla S, Briand C, Oualha M, Bendavid M, Beranger A, Benaboud S, Treluyer JM, Zheng Y, Capito C, Demir Z, Foissac F, Winter S, Gana I, Boujaafar S, Bouazza N, Hirt D, Antimicrob Agents Chemother 2020)

Reference: doi:10.1128/AAC.01426-20 (Antimicrob Agents Chemother 2020;64(12):e01426-20; Table 2).

**Model type: parametric population pharmacokinetic model** (nonlinear mixed-effects, SAEM, Monolix 2018R1). Suitable for simulation and MAP Bayesian estimation.

## Notes

- Study: prospective study (Optimome, Necker-Enfants Malades, Paris), 79 children (212 plasma concentrations, LC-MS/MS, LOQ 0.05 mg/L): 50 IV aciclovir, 22 oral (7 aciclovir, 22 valaciclovir tablets, often crushed), 7 both. Median (range) age 4.1 (0.02-18) years, weight 15 (3.1-66) kg, height 108 (49-169) cm, plasma creatinine 29 (10-172) umol/L, Schwartz eGFR 164 (56-399) mL/min/1.73 m2; 48 boys, 31 girls (Table 1). Median (range) valaciclovir dose 21 (17-63) mg/kg/day.
- The article models IV aciclovir, oral aciclovir and oral valaciclovir simultaneously. This file is the oral valaciclovir version (depot compartment, first-order absorption, F = 0.768). The IV version is `pediatrie/aciclovir_IV/models/ACV_Abdalla.Rmd`, with identical disposition parameters, covariates and IIV (the oral aciclovir route, F = 0.397, is not coded).
- Dose coding (explicit): `amt` is in mg of valaciclovir (tablet strength). The authors converted doses and concentrations to molar units ("dividing mass concentrations by the molarity of each compound", Methods) to fit aciclovir and valaciclovir jointly, so F = 0.768 is a molar bioavailability. The conversion is done in the model with MWR = 225.2/324.3 = 0.694 (molar mass of aciclovir / valaciclovir base).
- Structure: one-compartment model, first-order absorption (ka = 0.376 h-1, common to oral aciclovir and valaciclovir, no lag time), first-order elimination. Valaciclovir itself is not modelled (rapid presystemic conversion to aciclovir). Bioavailability: F = 1 x 0.768 for valaciclovir (Table 2 footnote: F = F x 0.768^OV x 0.397^OA).
- Covariates (Table 2 footnote): CL = 5.15 x (WT/15)^0.75 x (eGFR/164)^0.658; V = 16.2 x (WT/15) (allometric exponents fixed). The Methods give a median weight of 15.6 kg as the reference, whereas Table 1 and the final equations use 15 kg; 15 kg is used.
- eGFR is the Schwartz formula of the Methods, computed in the model: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = k x HT (cm) / SCR (mg/dL), with k = 0.45 if age < 2 years, 0.55 if 2-13 years or female >= 13 years, 0.7 if male >= 13 years; SCR is entered in umol/L and divided by 88.4. eGFR is captured.
- Default covariates: medians of Table 1: AGE 4.1 years, WT 15 kg, HT 108 cm, SCR 29 umol/L, SEX 1 (48 boys/31 girls). They give an eGFR of 181 mL/min/1.73 m2 (median of the study 164, the reference value of the model).
- IIV: Monolix SDs (Table 2): CL 0.389, V 0.434, squared: 0.1513 and 0.1884. IIV on ka and F could not be estimated (fixed to 0).
- Residual error: proportional, Monolix b = 0.48 (SD), variance 0.2304.
- Targets used by the authors: trough > 0.56 mg/L (HSV) or > 1.125 mg/L (VZV) and peak < 25 mg/L. With valaciclovir 20 mg/kg every 8 h, 95.2% and 75.3% of simulated children had a trough above 0.56 and 1.125 mg/L; proposed initial valaciclovir doses: 10-15 mg/kg every 6 h (eGFR < 250 mL/min/1.73 m2).
- Simulation check (typical 15 kg child, eGFR 164, steady state): valaciclovir 20 mg/kg every 8 h gives Cmax 5.1 and Cmin 2.1 mg/L, and 15 mg/kg every 6 h Cmax 4.6 and Cmin 2.7 mg/L.
- **Ambiguity:** with the molar conversion, the effective bioavailability per mg is 0.768 x 0.694 = 0.533 for valaciclovir versus 0.397 for oral aciclovir, so valaciclovir gives higher concentrations than the same mg/kg dose of oral aciclovir (Cmin 2.1 vs 1.6 mg/L at 20 mg/kg every 8 h), whereas the authors' simulations report slightly fewer children above 1.125 mg/L with valaciclovir (75.3%) than with oral aciclovir (85.9%); without conversion the difference would be even larger. **Choice:** the explicit molar conversion described in the Methods.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(mrgsolve)
library(mapbayr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r model}
code <- '
[PROB]
Abdalla et al. 2020 - aciclovir after oral valaciclovir in children (79 children, 212 samples after IV aciclovir,
oral aciclovir and oral valaciclovir, Monolix 2018R1 SAEM). One-compartment model, first-order absorption,
F = 0.768 (molar, dose converted with MWR). Covariates: weight (allometry) and Schwartz eGFR (computed from AGE, SEX, HT, SCR, power)
on CL, weight on V. IIV on CL and V. Proportional residual error.

[SET] end = 24, delta = 0.1

[PARAM] @annotated
TVCL     : 5.15  : Clearance for 15 kg and eGFR 164 mL/min/1.73 m2 (L/h)
TH_GFR   : 0.658 : Exponent of eGFR on CL
EGFR_REF : 164   : Reference eGFR, median (mL/min/1.73 m2)
WT_REF   : 15    : Reference weight (kg)
TVV      : 16.2  : Volume of distribution for 15 kg (L)
TVKA     : 0.376 : Absorption rate constant (1/h)
TVF      : 0.768 : Bioavailability of aciclovir from valaciclovir (molar)
MWR      : 0.694 : Molar mass ratio aciclovir/valaciclovir (225.2/324.3)
ETA1     : 0     : IIV CL
ETA2     : 0     : IIV V

[PARAM] @annotated @covariates
AGE : 4.1 : Age (years)
WT  : 15  : Body weight (kg)
HT  : 108 : Height (cm)
SCR : 29  : Serum creatinine (umol/L)
SEX : 1   : Sex (1 = male, 0 = female)

[CMT] @annotated
DEPOT : Depot, valaciclovir dose (mg) [ADM]
CENT  : Central compartment, aciclovir (mg) [OBS]

[MAIN]
double KSCH = 0.55;
if (AGE < 2) KSCH = 0.45;
if (AGE >= 13 && SEX == 1) KSCH = 0.7;
double EGFR = KSCH * HT / (SCR / 88.4);
double CL = TVCL * pow(WT / WT_REF, 0.75) * pow(EGFR / EGFR_REF, TH_GFR) * exp(ETA1 + ETA(1));
double V  = TVV * (WT / WT_REF) * exp(ETA2 + ETA(2));
double KA = TVKA;
F_DEPOT = TVF * MWR;

[ODE]
dxdt_DEPOT = -KA * DEPOT;
dxdt_CENT  =  KA * DEPOT - CL / V * CENT;

[OMEGA] @annotated
ECL : 0.1513 : IIV CL (variance, SD 0.389)
EV  : 0.1884 : IIV V (variance, SD 0.434)

[SIGMA] @annotated
PROP : 0.2304 : Proportional error (variance, b = 0.48)
ADD  : 0      : Additive error (mg/L), not estimated

[TABLE]
double IPRED = CENT / V;
double DV = IPRED * (1 + EPS(1)) + EPS(2);
int i = 0;
while (DV < 0 && i < 100) { simeps(); DV = IPRED * (1 + EPS(1)) + EPS(2); ++i; }

[CAPTURE] @annotated
DV   : Aciclovir plasma concentration (mg/L)
EGFR : Estimated GFR, Schwartz (mL/min/1.73 m2)
CL   : Individual clearance (L/h)
V    : Individual volume of distribution (L)
'
mod <- mcode("VACV_Abdalla", code)
```

```{r simulation}
# Typical 15 kg child (4.1 years, 108 cm, eGFR 164: SCR 32 umol/L), valaciclovir 20 mg/kg every 8 h and 15 mg/kg every 6 h, steady state
data <- data.frame(ID = 1:2, time = 0, evid = 1, cmt = 1, amt = c(20, 15) * 15, ii = c(8, 6), addl = c(11, 15), SCR = 32)

out <- mod %>%
  zero_re() %>%
  data_set(data) %>%
  mrgsim(end = 96, delta = 0.05) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  left_join(data %>% select(ID, ii), by = "ID") %>%
  filter(time >= 96 - ii) %>%
  mutate(time = time - (96 - ii), Regimen = factor(ID, labels = c("20 mg/kg q8h", "15 mg/kg q6h")))

# Article targets: trough > 0.56 / 1.125 mg/L, peak < 25 mg/L (Fig. 5)
out %>% group_by(Regimen) %>%
  summarise(EGFR = EGFR[1], CL = CL[1], Cmax = max(DV), Cmin = min(DV[time > 0]),
            AUCtau = sum(diff(time) * (head(DV, -1) + tail(DV, -1)) / 2))

ggplot(out, aes(time, DV, colour = Regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.56, 1.125), linetype = 2) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Aciclovir concentration (mg/L)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Abdalla et al. 2020 - oral valaciclovir, typical steady-state profiles")
```
